Inspect `scene3d.js`, `scene3d.css`, and `index.html` for syntax/runtime integration errors. 2. Run the game and capture/inspect a current screenshot; fix any rendering or layout defects. 3. Test starter selection, exploring, switching Pokémon, and mobile canvas interactions. ## Relevant Files - `scene3d.js`: New Three.js procedural scene and companion mesh models. - `scene3d.css`: New 3D canvas and overlay styles. - `index.html`: Canvas, stylesheet, Three.js CDN, and script wiring. - `game.js`: Existing game logic, updated to sync active partner/zone and exploration animation. ## Important Context - Changes are uncommitted. - Three.js is loaded from `https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/three@0.160.0/build/three.min.js`. - `scene3d.js` accesses `window.forest3d` from `game.js`; script ordering in `index.html` places it before `game.js`. - Existing HTML still includes `

- Transform the existing Pokémon forest game into a polished, playable 3D experience instead of relying on PNGs and CSS scenery.

- Build directly without asking clarifying questions; preserve the existing gameplay and UI.

- Turn the existing Pokémon forest game into a polished, playable 3D experience while preserving its gameplay and UI.

- Build directly without clarifying questions.
- Replace PNG/CSS scenery with 3D; preserve game mechanics and UI.
- Support drag-to-rotate, scroll-to-zoom, and exploration motion.

- Use Three.js for procedural forest geometry and modeled Pokémon companions.
- Keep existing game logic and connect it to the 3D scene through `window.forest3d`.

- Replaced the forest scene markup in `index.html` with a canvas and added Three.js/style/script wiring.

- Browser visual/gameplay checks are incomplete; Chromium reports no scene JavaScript errors, but gameplay interactions have not been tested.

1. Inspect the scene in the browser and verify starter selection displays the matching 3D companion.
